وَٱلْبَيْتِ ٱلْمَعْمُورِ
وَٱلسَّقْفِ ٱلْمَرْفُوعِ
وَٱلْبَحْرِ ٱلْمَسْجُورِ
إِنَّ عَذَابَ رَبِّكَ لَوَٰقِعٌ
مَّا لَهُۥ مِن دَافِعٍ
يَوْمَ تَمُورُ ٱلسَّمَآءُ مَوْرًا
وَتَسِيرُ ٱلْجِبَالُ سَيْرًا
فَوَيْلٌ يَوْمَئِذٍ لِّلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
ٱلَّذِينَ هُمْ فِى خَوْضٍ يَلْعَبُونَ
يَوْمَ يُدَعُّونَ إِلَىٰ نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ دَعًّا
هَٰذِهِ ٱلنَّارُ ٱلَّتِى كُنتُم بِهَا تُكَذِّبُونَ
أَفَسِحْرٌ هَٰذَآ أَمْ أَنتُمْ لَا تُبْصِرُونَ

إِنَّ ٱلْمُتَّقِينَ فِى جَنَّٰتٍ وَنَعِيمٍ
فَٰكِهِينَ بِمَآ ءَاتَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ وَوَقَىٰهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ عَذَابَ ٱلْجَحِيمِ
كُلُوا۟ وَٱشْرَبُوا۟ هَنِيٓـًٔۢا بِمَا كُنتُمْ تَعْمَلُونَ
مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ
وَٱلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُوا۟ وَٱتَّبَعَتْهُمْ ذُرِّيَّتُهُم بِإِيمَٰنٍ أَلْحَقْنَا بِهِمْ ذُرِّيَّتَهُمْ وَمَآ أَلَتْنَٰهُم مِّنْ عَمَلِهِم مِّن شَىْءٍ كُلُّ ٱمْرِئٍۭ بِمَا كَسَبَ رَهِينٌ
وَأَمْدَدْنَٰهُم بِفَٰكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا لَّا لَغْوٌ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌ
وَيَطُوفُ عَلَيْهِمْ غِلْمَانٌ لَّهُمْ كَأَنَّهُمْ لُؤْلُؤٌ مَّكْنُونٌ
وَأَقْبَلَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَىٰ بَعْضٍ يَتَسَآءَلُونَ
قَالُوٓا۟ إِنَّا كُنَّا قَبْلُ فِىٓ أَهْلِنَا مُشْفِقِينَ
فَمَنَّ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيْنَا وَوَقَىٰنَا عَذَابَ ٱلسَّمُومِ
إِنَّا كُنَّا مِن قَبْلُ نَدْعُوهُ إِنَّهُۥ هُوَ ٱلْبَرُّ ٱلرَّحِيمُ
فَذَكِّرْ فَمَآ أَنتَ بِنِعْمَتِ رَبِّكَ بِكَاهِنٍ وَلَا مَجْنُونٍ
أَمْ يَقُولُونَ شَاعِرٌ نَّتَرَبَّصُ بِهِۦ رَيْبَ ٱلْمَنُونِ
قُلْ تَرَبَّصُوا۟ فَإِنِّى مَعَكُم مِّنَ ٱلْمُتَرَبِّصِينَ
أَمْ تَأْمُرُهُمْ أَحْلَٰمُهُم بِهَٰذَآ أَمْ هُمْ قَوْمٌ طَاغُونَ
أَمْ يَقُولُونَ تَقَوَّلَهُۥ بَل لَّا يُؤْمِنُونَ
فَلْيَأْتُوا۟ بِحَدِيثٍ مِّثْلِهِۦٓ إِن كَانُوا۟ صَٰدِقِينَ
أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَٰلِقُونَ
أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
أَمْ عِندَهُمْ خَزَآئِنُ رَبِّكَ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْمُصَۣيْطِرُونَ
أَمْ لَهُمْ سُلَّمٌ يَسْتَمِعُونَ فِيهِ فَلْيَأْتِ مُسْتَمِعُهُم بِسُلْطَٰنٍ مُّبِينٍ
أَمْ لَهُ ٱلْبَنَٰتُ وَلَكُمُ ٱلْبَنُونَ
أَمْ تَسْـَٔلُهُمْ أَجْرًا فَهُم مِّن مَّغْرَمٍ مُّثْقَلُونَ
أَمْ عِندَهُمُ ٱلْغَيْبُ فَهُمْ يَكْتُبُونَ
أَمْ يُرِيدُونَ كَيْدًا فَٱلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا۟ هُمُ ٱلْمَكِيدُونَ
أَمْ لَهُمْ إِلَٰهٌ غَيْرُ ٱللَّهِ سُبْحَٰنَ ٱللَّهِ عَمَّا يُشْرِكُونَ
وَإِن يَرَوْا۟ كِسْفًا مِّنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ سَاقِطًا يَقُولُوا۟ سَحَابٌ مَّرْكُومٌ
فَذَرْهُمْ حَتَّىٰ يُلَٰقُوا۟ يَوْمَهُمُ ٱلَّذِى فِيهِ يُصْعَقُونَ
يَوْمَ لَا يُغْنِى عَنْهُمْ كَيْدُهُمْ شَيْـًٔا وَلَا هُمْ يُنصَرُونَ
وَإِنَّ لِلَّذِينَ ظَلَمُوا۟ عَذَابًا دُونَ ذَٰلِكَ وَلَٰكِنَّ أَكْثَرَهُمْ لَا يَعْلَمُونَ
وَٱصْبِرْ لِحُكْمِ رَبِّكَ فَإِنَّكَ بِأَعْيُنِنَا وَسَبِّحْ بِحَمْدِ رَبِّكَ حِينَ تَقُومُ
وَمِنَ ٱلَّيْلِ فَسَبِّحْهُ وَإِدْبَٰرَ ٱلنُّجُومِ

leads.title: Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses ↔ The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges
leads.summary: 1 correspondence read side by side: 1 same element.

evidence.text: Read side by side in both originals (alignments/hb-quran/07-hb-quran.yaml).

Shared motifs, rarest first: The prophet is no soothsayer (kahin), no madman, no poet awaiting the accident of fate (weight 6.0); Opponents accuse the prophet of forging lies against God (weight 6.0). Pair score 12.0.

Only in Levitical dues; forbidden divination; the prophet like Moses: Be wholehearted (tamim) with God; A prophecy that does not come true shows the prophet spoke presumptuously; Priest's due: shoulder, two cheeks and stomach of the sacrifice, and first of the fleece; Duty to accept a prophet God will send later [divergence between the texts]; How God's word reaches the prophet [divergence between the texts]; A future prophet promised in the earlier scripture [response between the texts]; A future prophet 'from among them' [divergence between the texts]; Where false words in a prophet's message come from, and what becomes of them [contrast between the texts]; Whether the dead may be consulted, or would persuade the living if they spoke [contrast between the texts]; False prophet put to death [divergence between the texts]; God sent before only men, inspired, from the people of the towns; Messengers are sent to people from among themselves; and 8 more.

Only in The Garden: offspring joined with parents, the cup without idle talk, youths like pearls; the run of 'or...?' challenges: The blessed question each other and recall that they used to be fearful among their families, and God saved them from the scorching wind (samum); In paradise they pass a cup to one another in which is no idle talk (laghw) or sin; If they saw a fragment of the sky falling they would say 'heaped-up clouds'; Glorify God when you rise, in the night, and at the retreat of the stars (dawn); Do they have a ladder (sullam) by which they eavesdrop on heaven? Let their listener bring clear proof; 'Be patient for your Lord's judgment, for you are under our eyes'; Were they created from nothing, or are they the creators? Did they create the heavens and earth?; Do they possess the Unseen (al-ghayb) so they write it down?; Dream of a ladder or stairway reaching heaven with angels ascending and descending; 'Eat and drink with relish for what you used to do'; A ladder (sullam / sullām) reaching from earth to heaven [divergence between the texts]; Believers' offspring who followed them in faith are joined with them in paradise, without loss of reward; each is pledged for what he earned; and 12 more.

matches.label: The blessed recline on couches set in rows (or face to face)

passages.text: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ
عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّوْضُونَةٍ
مُّتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَيْهَا مُتَقَٰبِلِينَ

sides.note: on jewel-woven couches, facing one another

matches.label: Abundant fruit in paradise from which the blessed eat

passages.text: وَأَمْدَدْنَٰهُم بِفَٰكِهَةٍ وَلَحْمٍ مِّمَّا يَشْتَهُونَ
وَفَٰكِهَةٍ مِّمَّا يَتَخَيَّرُونَ
وَفَٰكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ

matches.label: The blessed are paired with wide-eyed maidens (hur 'in)

passages.text: مُتَّكِـِٔينَ عَلَىٰ سُرُرٍ مَّصْفُوفَةٍ وَزَوَّجْنَٰهُم بِحُورٍ عِينٍ
وَحُورٌ عِينٌ
كَأَمْثَٰلِ ٱللُّؤْلُؤِ ٱلْمَكْنُونِ

matches.label: The effects of wine and of the cup: mockery, madness, or none

passages.text: يَتَنَٰزَعُونَ فِيهَا كَأْسًا لَّا لَغْوٌ فِيهَا وَلَا تَأْثِيمٌ

sides.note: Wine and its effects: lēṣ hay-yayin hōmeh šēḵār wə-ḵol šōḡeh bô lōʾ yeḥkām (wine is a mocker, strong drink a brawler) vs. yatanāzaʿūna fīhā kaʾsan lā laghwun fīhā wa-lā taʾthīm (a cup with no idle talk and no sin). The Quran's heavenly cup lacks just the faults Proverbs gives earthly wine.

passages.text: بِأَكْوَابٍ وَأَبَارِيقَ وَكَأْسٍ مِّن مَّعِينٍ
لَّا يُصَدَّعُونَ عَنْهَا وَلَا يُنزِفُونَ

sides.note: The effects of wine. Proverbs: ləmî ʾôy ... ləmî p̄əṣāʿîm ḥinnām ləmî ḥaḵlilûṯ ʿênāyim; la-məʾaḥărîm ʿal hay-yāyin; hikkûnî bal ḥālîtî ... māṯay ʾāqîṣ (woe, wounds, red eyes, stupor). Quran: bi-akwābin wa-abārīqa wa-kaʾsin min maʿīn, lā yuṣaddaʿūna ʿanhā wa-lā yunzifūn (no headache, no loss of wits). The Quran's paradise wine is described by the absence of the drunkard's woes.
